object_description: compact seven-story block with side loggias and roof terraces
design_condition: Placed across the plot, the block creates a natural forecourt at the main entrance and spacious lateral outdoor areas, while its compressed relationship with the existing school produces a convincing visual composition.

positive.statement: The placement creates an appropriate forecourt and lateral outdoor spaces with welcome spaciousness beside the compact building.
The four outdoor areas take on specific tasks and are designed accordingly.
The open-space design is well thought out, developed, and optimally tailored to the modest space available.
The central access zone allows both the main address and a side entrance, while the catering and multi-purpose areas connect well to the attractive outdoor space.
The classrooms are well lit and flexibly divisible because their long sides face the facade.
The spacious lounges and roof terraces offer a high-quality connection to the outdoors on each floor.
The loggias and structural hierarchy cleverly overplay the building's large scale and make the main entrance legible.
The additional connection to the sports hall ensures its operation outside school hours.

negative.statement: The outdoor-space concept lacks opportunities for retreat and staying.
The intermediate-climate rooms risk becoming too cold or too warm and therefore uncomfortable.
The spiral staircase is far too small for the number of students and provides poor vertical orientation in a zone with hardly any daylight.
The classroom floor heights are relatively low as a result of the seven-story structure.
The location of individual large trees above the sports hall is probably not entirely plausible.
The sports hall has no natural lighting.
